title: README
text:
highlight and highlight-current
Despite the default green, red, and blue, there are three colors available for this template:

forest green,
indian red, and
steel blue.

Code:
- <span class="fragment highlight-forestgreen" data-fragment-index="1">forest green</span>,
- <span class="fragment highlight-indianred" data-fragment-index="2">indian red</span>, and
- <span class="fragment highlight-steelblue" data-fragment-index="3">steel blue</span>.
Noted that, class fragment- with highlight-forestgreen, highlight-indianred, highlight-steelblue also highlight the fragment of current index with font-weight bold.

title: README
text:
highlight-current
Similar to the use of highlight, but the effects will disappear if next fragment index is triggered.
Code:
- <span class="fragment highlight-current-forestgreen" data-fragment-index="1">forest green</span>,
- <span class="fragment highlight-current-indianred" data-fragment-index="2">indian red</span>, and
- <span class="fragment highlight-current-steelblue" data-fragment-index="3">steel blue</span>.
Output:

forest green,
indian red, and
steel blue.

title: README
text:
highlight-bold and highlight-current-bold
When using highlight-bold and highlight-current-bold the original color is inherited. Both of them highlights the text with bold and slight shading.
Code:
- <span class="fragment highlight-current-bold" data-fragment-index="1">bold (current)</span>,
- <span class="fragment highlight-bold" data-fragment-index="2">bold (persistent)</span>, and
- <span class="fragment highlight-current-bold" data-fragment-index="3">bold (current)</span>

bold (current),
bold (persistent), and
bold (current)

Dealing with overflow
This is a scrollable page, with a scrollable container. Typically it is not a good idea to show a scrollable container in a scrollable page; this makes presenter struggle to scroll the correct target.
Scrollable container

title: README
text:
Dealing with overflow
Decision logic:

When Contents overflow:

Create a new slide with the same title with {.unlisted} (to not show repeat entries in TOC).
If 1. is not applicable (e.g., image itself overflow):

Use {.scrollable} on a single page. This way the Slide Heading (## <Slide Heading>) is not persistent on scroll.
When one needs the slide heading or some content on the top persist on scrolling, use Scrollable container.

title: How this website be built
text:
See https://quarto.org/docs/websites/


Quick Start





cd docs
quarto render --cache-refresh
See also:

.vscode/settings.json for livePreview settings
https://quarto.org/docs/websites/#config-file for setting up _quarto.yml
https://quarto.org/docs/websites/website-tools.html for Website tools
https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-web for the source code of how Quarto’s official website be built


⚠️ If you encounter slides/* file-not–fonud error in local rendering, manually run . docs/cpfiles.sh and render again.





Referring: https://quarto.org/docs/publishing/github-pages.html#publish-action


In bash,
cd docs
quarto publish gh-pages

This creates a new branch gh-pages, render files and publish them to e.g., https://okatsn.github.io/QuartoTemplates/
Noted that you have to go to the Github Settings => Pages => Deploy from a branch and Save.




See .github/workflows/deploy.yml.

title: Use Templates
text:
Documentation






By executing tree-slide.sh, you can create a new index.qmd file with all dependent files copied to the target directory; the scripts is intended to create a new presentation of tree-slide in the directory of ../HelloWorld at one click.
The script tree-slide.sh generates index.qmd files and others by calling tree-slide/render.js to render the mustache files therein with ./tree-slide/data.json, and copy them to ../HelloWorld, where your personal information should be set in tree-slide/data.json.


Clone QuartoTemplates to the directory of your projects:
git clone https://github.com/okatsn/QuartoTemplates.git
Modify data.json, and
cd QuartoTemplates
. tree-slide.sh HelloWorld




Alternatively, you can render file directly in ./tree-slide.
cd tree-slide
node render.js
